A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same p-mean portfolio research. Their complete main texts, proofs, experimental appendices, tables and figures are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original taxi, disaster-allocation and healthcare experiments, including approximation ratios, oracle-call counts and stakeholder outcomes.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments in those three domains and adds GPI comparison results and a taxi policy-diversity analysis.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the same portfolio construction, line search and budget-constrained selection procedures. The ESR/SER objectives and warm-start approach also remain unchanged. Expanded healthcare reward documentation does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four-route taxi environment, 12-cluster disaster-allocation problem and ARMMAN healthcare setting. The added comparisons and visualizations use existing coverage; the illustrative reward vectors are explanatory examples.

E2.justification: Appendix C and Table 3 add an evaluated GPI implementation attributed to Alegre et al. (2023), covering disaster allocation and healthcare. This introduces an algorithmic MORL comparator beyond the retained random policy and random p baselines and the proposed budgeted heuristic.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 changes the reported taxi policy space from a finite pretrained pool to all possible MDP policies, materially changing the described evaluation setting. Appendix E.4 also changes the budgeted heuristic's initial p from -ln(N)/ln(1/0.9) to -100. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 3 adds a taxi case study showing how portfolio policies distribute reward across routes, extending the policy-diversity analysis. The existing disaster visualization is retained as Figure 4 with revised labeling, rather than constituting a new experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 10 independent portfolios for the random baselines. v2 introduces no new repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty intervals or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 revise disaster and healthcare results and oracle counts: for example, disaster size-three approximation changes from 0.937 to 0.999, and size-four oracle calls from 43 to 50. The disaster size-five rows disappear, while taxi table values remain unchanged. Tables 3–4 add GPI scores and selected p values. Table 3 contains a conflicting disaster size-four score of 0.100 versus 1.000 in Tables 1–2.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds a claimed tighter bound immediately after Equation (8) in the proof of Theorem 4.1. The central portfolio guarantee, bounded-reward assumption, warm-start proposition and substantive proof framework are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, four contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about compact p-mean portfolios, approximation and computational guarantees, the budgeted heuristic and warm-starting. Added evidence does not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly explains why the budgeted heuristic or random p sampling can outperform p-MeanPortfolio, relating this to its approximation target and endpoint selection. The new Impact Statement explicitly limits the fairness coverage of p-means and clarifies that healthcare results involve no deployment.

D1.justification: v2 supplies an experiment-code repository link, distinguishes 59 healthcare stakeholder rewards from 200 balancing policies, and documents the alpha grid and smallest-alpha selection rule. Appendix C specifies SciPy differential evolution for GPI. These additions improve documentation without establishing changes to the underlying healthcare procedure.

R1.justification: v2 adds Yang et al. (2019), Reymond et al. (2022) and Alegre et al. (2023), with Appendix C comparing specific MORL approaches and stating an explicit first-of-its-kind claim. This expands the existing positioning against weighted-linear and Pareto approaches while retaining its central framing.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most method and proof prose remain intact. v2 locally rewrites motivation and results discussion, adds explanatory and impact sections, and moves experimental details from Appendix B to E around new Appendices B–D.

P2.justification: The main paper adopts a two-column conference layout, and Figure 1's panels become vertically stacked. v2 adds the p-mean illustration, taxi plot, GPI table and selected-p table. The retained disaster plot gains numerical p-axis labels and gridlines; the cluster-data table is retained as Table 5.

improvement.justification: The GPI comparison, clearer healthcare reward construction, reproducibility disclosures and explanation of baseline wins improve the paper's assessability. However, Table 3's 0.100 versus 1.000 discrepancy weakens reporting, and Table 1 still claims consistent superiority although random p sampling scores 0.832 against 0.706 for disaster size one. These inconsistencies limit the overall gain.
